Who We Are

Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,400 firms in nearly 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $9 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with nearly 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, London, Edinburgh, Pune, Dubai, Geneva, Singapore and São Paulo.

The Role

We are currently seeking a Director of Engineering for our Institutions Engineering Team. You will assume engineering leadership over our investor solutions and research product suite and take ownership of technology delivery across our Institutional segment and sophisticated investor product offerings.

You’ll lead a multi-disciplinary team of software engineers, platform architects, and engineering managers. The ideal candidate brings experience in Asset Management solutions, strong technical depth in scalable cloud-native systems and proven leadership in executing complex product roadmaps.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without requiring current or future visa sponsorship (for example, employment-based visas such as H-1B, F-1/OPT, or similar), and must be authorized to begin work in the U.S. on their first day of employment.

Strategic Leadership

Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering organization dedicated to the Institutional segment
Establish clear engineering goals, operational metrics, and delivery standards aligned with company objectives and create a high-performing engineering culture
Collaborate with Engineering, Product and Design leadership to drive Addepar strategy across all of our engineering organizations
Drive the technical vision, co-ordination and delivery across all products and solutions within our Institutional segment

Technology & Product Delivery

Partner closely with Product Management, Design, and GTM to define, prioritize, and execute product roadmaps
Implement robust Agile software development practices to ensure predictable, high-quality, and timely releases
Guide architectural decisions to ensure scalable, secure, and resilient system design suitable for institutional security and compliance standards
Champion engineering best practices, including automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and robust monitoring/observability platforms

Who You Are

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
8+ years of engineering leadership experience with a track record of managing managers, architects, and software engineers.
5+ years in Asset Management / Institutional Investing technology, including financial risk frameworks
Proven experience delivering enterprise software platforms with stringent security, regulatory, and uptime requirements
Deep familiarity with modern cloud architecture, microservices, API design, data pipelines, and enterprise security frameworks

$227,000—$355,000 USD

Act Like an Owner - Think and operate with intention, purpose and care. Own outcomes.
Build Together - Collaborate to unlock the best solutions. Deliver lasting value.
Champion Our Clients - Exceed client expectations. Our clients’ success is our success.
Drive Innovation - Be bold and unconstrained in problem solving. Transform the industry.
Embrace Learning - Engage our community to broaden our perspective. Bring a growth mindset.

We seek to bring together diverse ideas, experiences, skill sets, perspectives, backgrounds and identities to drive innovative solutions. We commit to promoting a welcoming environment where inclusion and belonging are held as a shared responsibility.

About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja
, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

At SharkNinja, we push the boundaries to develop world class consumer products that transform everyday life. The Director of Engineering - Motors, is a senior technical and people leader responsible for shaping the strategy, design, and development of advanced motor systems across SharkNinja’s growing product portfolio.

This is a player/coach role — you will lead and grow a team of motor engineers while staying hands-on with the most complex technical challenges. You bring deep expertise in electromagnetic design, electromechanical systems, and power conversion, and you excel at partnering with global motor suppliers to develop purpose-built solutions for our products. The ability to bridge rigorous technical depth with cross-functional and supplier collaboration is essential. Airflow and fluid-dynamics experience is a strong plus, particularly in applications involving fans, blowers, or high-performance suction systems.

What You’ll Do

Lead and develop a team of motor engineers — setting clear goals, fostering technical growth, and building a high-performing, collaborative engineering culture.
Drive motor technology strategy, defining the roadmap for motor architectures across SharkNinja’s product portfolio including BLDC, universal, and switched reluctance motors.
Provide technical oversight and guidance across end-to-end motor development from concept through prototype, validation, and production — working closely with motor manufacturers to ensure designs meet SharkNinja’s performance and quality requirements.
Partner deeply with global motor suppliers to co-develop optimized motor solutions, driving detailed design collaboration, component optimization, and production readiness.
Define and hold motor performance targets in partnership with cross-functional engineering teams — torque, speed, noise, vibration, efficiency, and thermal characteristics — aligned with product requirements.
Conduct and guide advanced electromagnetic and electromechanical analysis in partnership with cross-functional engineering teams, including FEA and simulation for magnetic circuits and rotor/stator design.
Collaborate closely with electrical, mechanical, controls, and firmware teams to ensure optimal motor integration, commutation algorithms, and drive efficiency.
Guide motor material selection, including laminations, magnets, winding specifications, and insulation systems.
Ensure design for manufacturability (DFM) and scalability in partnership with suppliers and manufacturing partners.
Collaborate with airflow and mechanical design teams on system-level performance where fluid dynamics interact with motor behavior.
Contribute to SharkNinja’s technology roadmap in motor and actuation systems, representing the motors function in senior leadership forums.

What You’ll Bring

15+ years of experience in motor design and development, ideally in consumer products, appliances, or electromechanical systems — with demonstrated experience in a technical leadership or management role.
Proven people leadership skills — experience building, mentoring, and developing engineering teams.
Expert-level understanding of electromagnetic theory, motor physics, and magnetic material properties.
Hands-on experience with FEA tools (e.g., Maxwell, JMAG, Motor-CAD) for electromagnetic and thermal modeling.
Strong background in electrical machine design, including stator winding, rotor dynamics, and torque ripple optimization.
Deep knowledge of motor control principles, including sensorless and vector control, PWM techniques, and inverter systems.
Extensive supplier partnership experience — driving detailed design collaboration, refinement, and production readiness with global motor suppliers.
Experience working with Asian motor suppliers, particularly in managing design collaboration, communication, and development cycles across time zones and cultural contexts.
Familiarity with manufacturing processes for motors (stamping, winding, potting, balancing).
Airflow and fluid-dynamics experience is highly advantageous.
Proven cross-functional collaborator across mechanical, electrical, and firmware disciplines.
Strong communication, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to influence at senior levels.
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering required; Master’s or Ph.D. preferred with emphasis in electromagnetics or motor systems.

drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home.

with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community.

Key Responsibilities

System Design & Architecture – System Scalability:

Manages the development and implementation of scalable distributed systems and components across multiple teams, including the effective use of distributed state management tools.
Oversees code and/or system optimization efforts for large-scale data processing and high-throughput requirements within and across teams to support hyper-scale systems.
Guides teams to define scalability requirements for owned components and ensures design and implementation requirements are met.
Manages the use of data plane platforms to effectively handle large-scale data retrieval, storage, and processing.
Ensures team accurately designs performance and load testing.

System Design & Architecture – System Reliability Design:

Manages the strategy for building fault-tolerant components and systems capable of withstanding in-service updates by guiding the implementation of redundancy, replication, and automatic failover mechanisms.
Develops design strategies for systems to effectively handle service disruptions (e.g., network partitions) by prioritizing consistency, availability, or partition tolerance.
Leads implementation and optimization initiatives across teams for approaches to handle network unreliability, including load-shedding, throttling, and rate-limiting.
Guides teams to design components and systems that are durable and adhere to service level objectives (SLOs), setting expectations for availability and durability of other computing services within the department.

Provides oversight in defining key performance indicators (KPIs) and telemetry to identify gaps or issues in running systems.
Oversees the building and customization of moderately complex dashboards, telemetry systems, and alerting mechanisms to proactively monitor components and system health.

System Design & Architecture – Correctness / Availability:

Oversees the design and implementation of functional and correctness requirements for feature sets and/or systems in new or existing systems.
Guides teams to design complex test scenarios (e.g., fault-injection, brown-out) to evaluate system correctness.
Directs implementation strategies for data replication and synchronization techniques to maintain data integrity and availability.

is a newly created, executive-level position with a clear mandate: architect a unified AI strategy, build a world-class engineering team, and deliver production-grade AI at scale across the operational nerve center of a global bank. This is not a coordination or advisory role. It is a builder's role — one with the budget, the mandate, and the organizational reach to make it real.

You will own the AI strategy and delivery capability across a $200M+ technology portfolio spanning some of the most operationally complex domains in banking: KYC, fraud detection, wholesale lending operations, global reconciliations, cash management, payments control, non-financial regulatory reporting, payroll, and international operations
. The scale is significant, the problems are highly complex at this stage, and the impact is direct — the solutions you build will influence how trillions of dollars in transactions flow daily, how regulatory risk is managed, and how Citi's operational infrastructure evolves over the next decade.

Unlike a role at a pure-play technology company, you will be solving AI challenges where failure has regulatory and systemic consequence — and where success reshapes the economics and resilience of critical global operations. The ambiguity is real, the stakes are high, and the opportunity for lasting impact is unmatched.

This role reports directly to the Head of COO Technology.

Responsibilities:

AI Strategy & Platform Architecture:

Define and own the multi-year AI strategy for the COO Technology portfolio; translate business intent into a concrete, milestone-driven execution roadmap with measurable outcomes
Develop architecture blueprints and end-to-end systems design for Generative AI and agentic workflows across diverse operational domains
Build the shared AI platform — reusable models, tooling, guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and accelerators — that reduces duplication, lowers cost, and enables faster adoption across COO
Establish and enforce engineering standards, architectural guardrails, and development patterns across all AI initiatives
Define a rigorous total cost of ownership model for developing, deploying, and sustaining AI in production
Identify and evaluate emerging GenAI technologies, foundation models, and agent frameworks — and make deliberate, defensible decisions on where to build, buy, or partner

Production AI Delivery at Enterprise Scale

Lead end-to-end delivery of AI solutions across high-complexity, regulated operational environments — from architecture through production deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement
Drive the agentic product development lifecycle: runtime harness design, evaluation frameworks, human-in-the-loop workflows, feedback loops, and production readiness criteria
Manage cross-functional delivery spanning engineering, product, data, architecture, cyber, risk & compliance, and operations
Proactively identify and resolve dependencies, critical path risks, and systemic delivery blockers; ensure on-time, on-budget execution
Ensure all AI solutions meet production-grade standards: stability, scalability, auditability, explainability, and regulatory compliance

Executive Partnership & AI Governance

Serve as the senior AI executive point of contact for COO function leads — partnering directly with the Heads of Core Operations Technology, Shared Services Technology, and Controls Technology
Lead AI governance forums and Architecture Review Boards; establish clear decision rights and review cadences across the portfolio
Translate complex technical realities into clear, compelling narratives for senior non-technical audiences — including COO, CIO, and regulatory stakeholders
Develop executive-level communications — steering committee materials, portfolio dashboards, and milestone tracking — that improve decision velocity and reduce execution risk
Ensure full adherence to Citi's internal policies, risk and control frameworks, model risk management (MRM) standards, and applicable regulatory requirements

Building the AI Engineering Organization

Build, structure, and lead a high-performing AI engineering function aligned to COO's operational priorities — including team topology, operating model, and career pathways
Foster a culture of technical excellence, intellectual curiosity, and pragmatic innovation: engineers who ship production solutions, not prototypes
Own and manage the AI technology portfolio budget (~$200M), driving disciplined funding allocation, financial transparency, and cost-to-serve accountability
Lead productivity and efficiency programs with measurable targets across cycle time, quality, throughput, and engineering leverage
Define and optimize vendor and partner strategy, including strategic AI platform partnerships (e.g., Google, Anthropic), third-party tooling, and outsourced delivery models

15+ years of experience in Technology - Required:

Generative AI & LLM Engineering: Deep, hands-on expertise in large language models including model selection, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), vector database design, and evaluation methodologies. You understand how models behave in production, not just in demos.
Agentic Systems Design: Proven experience designing and deploying multi-agent architectures and orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI); tool-use patterns, human-in-the-loop workflows, and agentic safety at enterprise scale
AI/ML Engineering & MLOps: Full AI/ML lifecycle ownership: training pipelines, model deployment, versioning, monitoring, drift detection, observability (e.g., Weights & Biases, Arize), and lifecycle management using platforms such as MLflow, Vertex AI, or SageMaker
Cloud AI Platforms: Demonstrated deployment of AI workloads on AWS, GCP, and/or Azure including managed ML services, scalable inference infrastructure, and vector stores
Programming & Frameworks: Strong Python proficiency; working knowledge of PyTorch or TensorFlow; applied experience with AI application frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, or equivalents)
Enterprise AI Architecture: Designing AI systems for regulated production environments: data security, model explainability, audit logging, access controls, and integration with legacy systems

Leadership & Delivery - Required:

15+ years in technology, with a proven record of leading large-scale engineering organizations through build-out and transformation
10+ years of management experience, including direct leadership of senior engineers and architects, and management of managers across global teams
Demonstrated delivery of enterprise AI solutions with realized measurable business outcomes — not just successful pilots or proofs of concept
Experience managing large, complex technology budgets ($50M+) with accountability for financial transparency and ROI
Track record of operating effectively in matrixed, cross-functional organizations at the intersection of technology and operations

Domain & Contextual Knowledge - Strongly Preferred

Deep familiarity with financial services operations and the regulatory landscape — particularly KYC/AML, fraud, reconciliations, and regulatory reporting
Strong understanding of model risk management (MRM) and what it takes to move AI from development to production under regulatory scrutiny
Experience engaging with strategic technology partners (cloud providers, AI platform companies) at an executive level

Leadership Profile

You build platforms, not point solutions — you instinctively seek the reusable, the shared, the scalable
You are equally credible in a deep technical architecture review and a board-level strategy discussion
You attract, develop, and retain strong technical talent — engineers want to work for you because they grow
You operate with clarity and urgency in ambiguous environments; complexity energizes rather than paralyzes you
You communicate with precision — you can make a complex AI architecture concept land with a CRO, a COO, and a principal engineer, and you do it differently for each

Education:

Bachelors required; Master's in CS, AI/ML, or related field preferred

What success looks like:

Establish the AI engineering team and operating model — hire and structure a high-performing team with clear roles, responsibilities, and a strong culture
Deliver 3+ production-grade agentic AI systems across priority COO domains, with measurable operational impact (cost, speed, quality, or risk reduction)

Greenfield mandate. The team, the platform, and the strategy are yours to define. You will set the architectural direction, the engineering culture, and the standards that govern AI across the COO portfolio.

added.title: Senior Manager, Network Security Engineering
added.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Network Security Engineering leads a team of security architects and engineers responsible for designing, implementing, and operating McKesson's enterprise network security capabilities. This role sits at the intersection of technology and business, translating enterprise risk, compliance, and business requirements into scalable, secure network architectures across on-premises, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments.

The ideal candidate is a strategic leader who combines deep technical credibility with strong people leadership, capable of building trusted-advisor relationships across IT, Cybersecurity, Cloud, Application, and Business teams. All security solutions are tested, documented, and validated prior to deployment, reinforcing the Network Design and Engineering team's reputation as a trusted advisor to McKesson's customers and supporting business units.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, coach, and develop a team of network security architects and engineers, fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Provide technical mentorship and career development pathways for team members, building bench strength and succession readiness.
Build and manage the team's operating rhythm, workload prioritization, and performance goals in alignment with department objectives.

Strategy & Business Alignment

Shape and communicate a multi-year network security strategy and roadmap that anticipates future technology needs and aligns with enterprise business goals.
Translate business requirements and risk priorities into clear technical requirements, architecture decisions, and engineering execution plans.
Partner with business and IT cross-functional stakeholders, including Cybersecurity, Cloud, IT Operations, Network Operations, and IAM teams, to ensure network security initiatives support broader business transformation objectives.
Build strong relationships with senior leadership, presenting strategic recommendations, investment priorities, and risk trade-offs in business terms.

Architecture & Engineering

Design and implement robust, future-ready network security architectures that meet performance, scalability, and regulatory compliance requirements.
Integrate Zero Trust principles, micro-segmentation, and identity-based access controls across hybrid and multi-cloud environments (Azure and Google Cloud).
Oversee deployment and lifecycle management of advanced security technologies, including next-generation firewalls, Zscaler, Network Access Control, IDS/IPS, and SD-WAN across both IT and OT networks.
Drive network automation initiatives to improve consistency, reduce manual effort, and accelerate secure delivery of infrastructure changes.
Plan, design, and execute infrastructure upgrades, expansions, and optimizations that improve performance, resiliency, and reliability.

Operations, Risk & Compliance

Develop and maintain network security strategies, standards, and operational best practices to ensure secure, scalable, and compliant network operations.
Lead infrastructure security evaluations, control testing, and incident response efforts, driving continuous improvement in overall security posture.
Lead troubleshooting for complex, escalated network issues, ensuring rapid resolution of outages and performance bottlenecks.
Ensure compliance with applicable industry standards and frameworks (NIST, ISO 27001, CIS Controls) and internal cybersecurity policy.
Maintain accurate network security documentation, including architecture diagrams, configuration standards, and operational runbooks.
Evaluate emerging networking and security technologies, recommending enhancements that improve efficiency, resilience, and risk posture.

What We're Looking For

We are seeking a strategic thinker with deep technical credibility, strong people leadership, and the business acumen to translate risk and business requirements into scalable, secure solutions.

Minimum Requirements

Typically requires 9+ years of progressive network security engineering experience, including 3+ years of supervisory or management experience building and leading technical teams.

Critical Skills

Demonstrated ability to translate business and regulatory requirements into technical architecture and engineering roadmaps.
Strong expertise in enterprise networking technologies, including routing, switching, wireless, next-generation firewalls, and cybersecurity.
Hands-on experience implementing cybersecurity frameworks and network security controls at enterprise scale.
Proven experience securing hybrid and multi-cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP), including Zero Trust and identity-based access models.
Proficiency with network and security monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting tools to support proactive risk management.
Track record of building trusted, consultative relationships with business stakeholders, peers, and senior leadership.

Leadership & Business Acumen

Executive-level communication skills, with the ability to present complex technical risk in clear business terms to senior leadership and non-technical stakeholders.
Experience managing budgets, vendor relationships, and cross-functional project delivery.
Demonstrated success building high-performing teams through coaching, mentorship, and structured professional development.
Strong problem-solving skills, sound judgment under pressure, and comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.

Preferred Certifications

Security certifications such as CISSP, CISM, PCNSE, ZCCP, CCSP, or Azure/AWS Security certifications are a plus.

Education

Minimum Master's degree, Information Security, Cybersecurity or equivalent professional experience with relevant certifications.

added.title: Senior Manager - Blockchain Security & Digital Asset Infrastructure
added.description:
Location: New York, Charlotte, Chicago, St. Louis, Boston

At EY, we’re all in to shape your future with confidence.

We’ll help you succeed in a globally connected powerhouse of diverse teams and take your career wherever you want it to go. Join EY and help to build a better working world.

At EY, you’ll have the chance to build a career as unique as you are, with the global scale, support, inclusive culture, and technology to become the best version of you. We’re counting on your unique voice and perspective to help EY become even better, too. Join us and build an exceptional experience for yourself, and a better working world for all.

The Opportunity

EY’s Blockchain & Digital Assets practice is seeking a highly experienced Senior Manager to serve as a lead technical architect and trusted advisor for institutional clients navigating the rapidly evolving digital asset ecosystem. This role combines deep technical expertise in cryptography, cybersecurity, and digital asset custody with strategic advisory capabilities to help organizations safeguard digital assets against traditional cyber threats and emerging AI-enabled attack vectors.

The successful candidate will possess extensive hands-on experience designing, implementing, and securing institutional-grade digital asset infrastructure. This individual will work directly with leading financial institutions, digital asset custodians, exchanges, and crypto-native organizations to develop resilient trust architectures and infrastructure security strategies.

Your Key Responsibilities

Infrastructure Safeguarding: Design, assess, and audit institutional-grade digital asset custody solutions, including Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), and air-gapped cold storage environments.
Protocol Analysis: Conduct technical evaluations of Bitcoin, Ethereum, and emerging Layer 1 and Layer 2 ecosystems, with emphasis on security assumptions, consensus mechanisms, attack vectors, and operational risks.
AI-Driven Threat Modeling: Develop defensive strategies to address AI-assisted cybersecurity risks, including autonomous vulnerability discovery and multi-stage attack scenarios.
Cryptographic Implementation: Provide subject matter expertise in Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs), threshold signature schemes, and distributed key management systems.
Incident Response & Engineering: Lead technical incident response efforts during active security events, coordinating engineering and security teams to contain threats and strengthen infrastructure resilience.
Strategic Advisory: Translate complex technical risks into actionable business intelligence for C-suite stakeholders, with focus on infrastructure trust models and the long-term utility of verifiable digital assets.
Practice Development: Lead complex client engagements, manage cross-functional teams, and support business development through thought leadership, market insights, and client pursuits.

Skills And Attributes For Success

Deep understanding of institutional digital asset custody frameworks and key management practices.
Strong technical expertise in blockchain protocols, cryptographic architectures, and cybersecurity engineering.
Ability to communicate complex technical concepts effectively to both technical and executive audiences.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and incident response capabilities.
Experience leading large-scale client engagements and managing diverse technical teams.
Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in fast-paced, high-stakes environments.

To Qualify for the Role, You Must Have

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline.
Minimum of 8 years of experience in cybersecurity, systems engineering, blockchain security, digital asset infrastructure, or cryptographic research.
Demonstrated hands-on experience managing private key lifecycles, digital asset custody operations, signing ceremonies, and enterprise-scale key management programs.
Deep knowledge of Bitcoin and Ethereum architecture, including the Bitcoin UTXO model, Bitcoin Script, Lightning Network, EVM, account abstraction, validator operations, and staking mechanisms.
Strong understanding of security models and architectural trade-offs across blockchain ecosystems such as Solana, Cosmos, and Polkadot.
Advanced knowledge of cryptographic primitives and protocols, including SHA-256, Keccak, ECDSA, Schnorr signatures, Multi-Party Computation (MPC), and threshold signature schemes.
Experience with traditional cybersecurity domains, including Linux security, network segmentation and isolation, application and API security, and infrastructure hardening.
Experience leveraging generative AI and large language models (LLMs) for security analysis, threat detection, vulnerability assessment, and code review activities.
Experience leading technical teams and delivering complex client-facing projects.

Ideally, You’ll Also Have

Master's degree in computer science, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, Engineering, or related field.
Advanced cybersecurity, blockchain security, or cryptography certifications.
Experience within a professional services, consulting, or advisory organization.
Thought leadership contributions through industry publications, speaking engagements, open-source projects, or blockchain security research.
Strong understanding of regulatory and operational risk considerations impacting digital asset custody platforms and financial institutions.
Experience working with global financial services organizations, asset managers, custodians, exchanges, or fintech firms.

What We Look For

We’re looking for individuals who combine deep technical expertise with strategic business acumen. The ideal candidate is passionate about securing the future of digital assets, understands that infrastructure and operational controls are at the core of trust, and can help clients navigate complex cybersecurity and digital asset risks in an increasingly AI-driven landscape.

What We Offer You

At EY, we’ll develop you with future-focused skills and equip you with world-class experiences. We’ll empower you in a flexible environment, and fuel you and your extraordinary talents in a diverse and inclusive culture of globally connected teams. Learn more.

We offer a comprehensive compensation and benefits package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to the business. The base salary range for this job in all geographic locations in the US is $150,400 to $343,600. The base salary range for New York City Metro Area, Washington State and California (excluding Sacramento) is $180,500 to $390,500. Individual salaries within those ranges are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge, skills and geography. In addition, our Total Rewards package includes medical and dental coverage, pension and 401(k) plans, and a wide range of paid time off options.
Join us in our team-led and leader-enabled hybrid model. Our expectation is for most people in external, client serving roles to work together in person 40-60% of the time over the course of an engagement, project or year.
Under our flexible vacation policy, you’ll decide how much vacation time you need based on your own personal circumstances. You’ll also be granted time off for designated EY Paid Holidays, Winter/Summer breaks, Personal/Family Care, and other leaves of absence when needed to support your physical, financial, and emotional well-being.
